text:
Marathon Petroleum stock has climbed 0.69% today and 9.59% over the past two weeks, riding a sharp rally that accelerated from September 14th onward. The immediate driver is the tight energy market: US crude oil is trading at $107 per barrel, global crude has spiked to $130, and US refineries are running flat-out at 96.8% capacity. With diesel and heating oil inventories sitting at just 107.9 million barrels—well below comfortable levels—refiners like Marathon are processing crude at maximum rates and earning strong margins on every barrel they turn into fuel.

Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are keeping crude elevated and supply concerns alive. Recent reports of attacks near Saudi Arabia's main airport and exchanges with the Houthis have spooked the market, even though the initial Saudi pipeline damage proved less disruptive than feared. Combined with record diesel prices already squeezing the transportation sector and the broader economy, this environment rewards refiners with strong operational leverage: they buy crude at high prices but sell finished products into an even tighter market.
